title: Acute diarrhoea with dehydration in children
subject: paediatrics
summary: Classify dehydration as none, some or severe and treat with WHO plans: extra ORS after each stool, low-osmolarity ORS 75 mL/kg over 4 hours, or IV Ringer lactate 100 mL/kg over 3 to 6 hours by age. Give zinc, continue feeding, and give antibiotics only for bloody diarrhoea or suspected cholera.

sections.title: Classify dehydration (WHO / IMNCI)
items: Severe dehydration: two or more of lethargy or unconsciousness, sunken eyes, unable to drink or drinking poorly, skin pinch goes back very slowly (2 seconds or more).
Some dehydration: two or more of restlessness or irritability, sunken eyes, drinks eagerly or thirsty, skin pinch goes back slowly.
No dehydration: not enough signs to classify as some or severe dehydration.

Also look for blood in stool (dysentery), diarrhoea for 14 days or more (persistent diarrhoea), severe acute malnutrition (use the SAM protocol, not these plans), abdominal mass or distension, and attacks of crying with pallor in infants (intussusception).

sections.title: Plan C: severe dehydration
items: Start IV fluid immediately; give ORS by mouth while the drip is set up if the child can drink. Use Ringer lactate (0.9% saline if unavailable); 5% dextrose alone is not effective.

Give 100 mL/kg: under 12 months, 30 mL/kg over 1 hour then 70 mL/kg over 5 hours; 12 months to 5 years, 30 mL/kg over 30 minutes then 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours. Repeat the first 30 mL/kg once if the radial pulse is still weak or absent.
Reassess every 15 to 30 minutes and run faster if not improving. Start ORS about 5 mL/kg/h once the child can drink (usually after 3 to 4 hours in infants, 1 to 2 hours in children).
Reassess infants after 6 hours and children after 3 hours, reclassify, and continue with Plan A, B or C.

If IV fluid cannot be given and IV care is not available within 30 minutes: ORS by nasogastric tube 20 mL/kg/h for 6 hours (120 mL/kg), reassessing every 1 to 2 hours; refer urgently if not improving after 3 hours.

sections.title: Plan B: some dehydration
items: Give low-osmolarity ORS about 75 mL/kg over 4 hours in the facility. By weight: under 6 kg 200 to 400 mL; 6 to under 10 kg 400 to 700 mL; 10 to under 12 kg 700 to 900 mL; 12 to 19 kg 900 to 1400 mL. Give more if the child wants.
Give small frequent sips from a cup or spoon (a teaspoon every 1 to 2 minutes under 2 years). If the child vomits, wait 10 minutes and continue more slowly. Continue breastfeeding.
Reassess after 4 hours: Plan A if no dehydration, repeat Plan B if still some dehydration, Plan C if severe dehydration has developed.

sections.title: Plan A, zinc and feeding
items: Extra fluid after each loose stool: under 2 years 50 to 100 mL, 2 years or older 100 to 200 mL, as ORS, clean water or food-based fluids. Give 2 ORS packets for home and teach mixing.

Zinc for every child with diarrhoea, started early: 10 mg daily under 6 months and 20 mg daily at 6 months or older for 10 to 14 days (14 days in India's national programme). WHO 2024 conditionally suggests 5 mg daily to reduce vomiting.
Continue breastfeeding and age-appropriate feeding throughout; give an extra meal daily for 2 weeks after recovery.
Return immediately if drinking poorly, becoming sicker, developing fever or blood in stool; review in 5 days if not improving.

sections.title: Antibiotics: only for specific indications
items: Do not give antibiotics for acute watery diarrhoea (WHO 2024), and do not give antidiarrhoeal drugs or antiemetics to young children.

Dysentery (visible blood in stool): ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg orally twice daily for 3 days (max 500 mg per dose); second line or severely ill, ceftriaxone 50 to 80 mg/kg IV/IM once daily for 3 days. Follow local Shigella susceptibility and review after 2 days.

Suspected cholera (acute watery diarrhoea with severe dehydration during a local outbreak, usually over 2 years): add an oral antibiotic to which local Vibrio cholerae is sensitive, such as single-dose azithromycin 20 mg/kg (max 1 g).
Admit infants under 2 months with dysentery, children with dysentery and SAM, and toxic, lethargic or distended children. Examine infants with blood in stool for intussusception.

sections.title: Monitoring
items: During IV rehydration watch pulse volume, capillary refill, consciousness, urine output and signs of overhydration (puffy eyelids, rising respiratory rate, crackles, enlarging liver).
Check electrolytes and glucose in severe dehydration, altered sensorium, convulsions or suspected hypernatraemia. Routine stool culture is not needed.
Observe for at least 6 hours after rehydration to confirm the carer can maintain hydration with ORS.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Using standard ORS or rapid IV boluses in children with severe acute malnutrition; they need ReSoMal and the SAM shock protocol.
Routine metronidazole or other antibiotics for watery diarrhoea.
Withholding feeds or breastfeeding during diarrhoea.
Missing hypernatraemia (irritability, doughy skin) or intussusception (blood in stool, abdominal mass, intermittent crying).

drugs.name: Low-osmolarity ORS
drugs.dose: Plan B: 75 mL/kg over 4 hours; Plan A: 50 to 100 mL (under 2 years) or 100 to 200 mL (2 years or older) after each loose stool
drugs.notes: Nasogastric 20 mL/kg/h for 6 hours if IV fluids are not possible in severe dehydration.

drugs.name: Ringer lactate
drugs.dose: 100 mL/kg IV: under 12 months 30 mL/kg over 1 hour then 70 mL/kg over 5 hours; 12 months to 5 years 30 mL/kg over 30 minutes then 70 mL/kg over 2.5 hours
drugs.notes: Use 0.9% saline if Ringer lactate is unavailable.

drugs.name: Zinc
drugs.dose: Under 6 months 10 mg once daily; 6 months or older 20 mg once daily; for 10 to 14 days
drugs.notes: Dissolve in breast milk, ORS or water. WHO 2024 suggests 5 mg daily as an alternative.

drugs.name: Ciprofloxacin
drugs.dose: 15 mg/kg orally every 12 hours for 3 days (max 500 mg per dose)

drugs.name: Ceftriaxone
drugs.dose: 50 to 80 mg/kg IV/IM once daily for 3 days (max 2 g per day)
drugs.notes: Second line for dysentery or severely ill children.

drugs.name: Azithromycin
drugs.dose: 20 mg/kg orally as a single dose (max 1 g)
drugs.notes: Suspected cholera; choose according to local susceptibility.
